metadata.title: Create your mattress | asleep
metadata.description: Configure your asleep Original mattress: pick a size, tell us your weight and sleep preference, and see the recommended firmness.

sizeHint: We recommend allowing 20 cm more than your height.
partnerWeightTitle: Weight and sleep preference of partner
mindTheGapBody: For this combination we recommend two single mattresses. The top layer of a double asleep is not split, so a large firmness difference between sides can feel like a ridge in the middle.
resultSolo: This is the setup we recommend for you.
resultMatch: You make a great pair — one double mattress, with each side set to the comfort you each prefer.
resultNoMatch: Your firmness settings are too far apart for one double mattress. We recommend two singles so each of you can sleep on your own setup.

advice.text: This is the most yielding setup. Side sleepers and lighter bodies usually feel the most pressure relief here, with the shoulders and hips able to sink in.
advice.more: If you wake up on your side and like a plush, cloud-like feel, start here. You can always unzip asleep later and step up a level if you want more support.

advice.text: A plush feel with a little more structure underneath. Good if you want softness without losing alignment.
advice.more: This is a common choice for mixed sleep positions. If extra soft feels like too much sink, this is the next step up.

advice.text: asleep arrives in this configuration. It balances cushioning and support for most sleepers and sleeping positions.
advice.more: If you are unsure, sleep on this setup first. After a few nights you can unzip the cover and turn a layer if you want it softer or firmer.

advice.text: A step firmer than the default. You still get some give on top, with a more stable base for the hips and lower back.
advice.more: Back sleepers and people who like a 'on the mattress' feel often land here. It is also a good middle ground when two sleepers are close but not identical.

advice.text: A supportive setup with less sink. Back and stomach sleepers, and heavier bodies, often prefer this.
advice.more: If you tend to overheat or dislike a hug from the foam, firmer layers keep you higher on the surface while the comfort zones still follow your spine.

advice.text: The most supportive combination. Choose this if you want to lie on top of the mattress rather than in it.
advice.more: This is the setup for people who like a very stable, hotel-firm feel. You can still move a layer later if it turns out to be more than you need.
